https://www.politico.eu/article/european.text: Former European Parliament President Klaus Hänsch has died, current Parliament President Roberta Metsola confirmed on Wednesday. “His Parliament mourns the loss of a champion of Europe, who took office at a time of profound change for our continent, and who never stopped believing in the potential of this project,” wrote Metsola in a social media post . “At our last meeting just a few weeks ago, his unwavering optimism shone through as he described his ongoing efforts to promote civic engagement and nurture young European leaders. Europe will miss him. May he rest in peace,” she added. Hänsch, a German Social Democrat, served as Parliament president from 1994 to 1997, and was an MEP from 1979 to 2009. He was 87 years old. By Jazmin Logan August 10, 2026 10:48 am Facebook X More LinkedIn Email SMS Clarksville Now Dalton Eatherly in court on May 29, 2026. (Jazmin Logan) Updated with information from the Davidson County bond hearing. CLARKSVILLE, TN ( CLARKSVILLE NOW ) – The social media influencer charged in the May 13 shooting outside the Montgomery County Courts Center has bonded out of jail. Dalton Levi Eatherly, 28 – known online as “Chud the Builder” – is charged with attempted murder, employing a firearm during the commission of a dangerous felony, aggravated assault, and reckless endangerment with a deadly weapon. Eatherly had been in custody for nearly three months, however the Montgomery County Jail confirmed to Clarksville Now that Eatherly was released a couple of days ago. Scene after shots fired outside Montgomery County Courthouse on May 13, 2026. (Jazmin Logan) Montgomery County Courthouse shooting On May 13 at about 1:15 p.m., Eatherly got in a confrontation in Millennium Plaza, according to previous reports . The arrest warrant obtained by Clarksville Now alleges Eatherly and another man, identified as Joshua Fox, got into a verbal confrontation. Eatherly then “turned his body in a bladed stance” and reached for a firearm in his jacket pocket. “Thereafter, a physical altercation ensued,” said the warrant. Investigators said Eatherly then fired multiple shots, striking Fox several times. Fox was flown by LifeFlight to Vanderbilt University Medical Center and underwent emergency surgery. Fox is now out of the hospital and slowly recovering, according to his mother, Carolyn Smith. She told Clarksville Now in June that the bullets fractured some of his ribs and left him with ongoing breathing issues and mental trauma, according to previous reports . Smith urged the community to de-escalate tensions and stop issuing threats toward judges, attorneys, her family and Eatherly’s family. Dalton Eatherly, aka “Chud the Builder,” after shots were fired outside Montgomery County Courthouse on May 13, 2026. (Contributed) Eatherly also shot himself in the arm during the struggle, and he was taken to Vanderbilt Clarksville Hospital for treatment, according to previous reports . At the time of the shooting, Eatherly was already out on bond in two other cases – a harassment case in Montgomery County bound over to the grand jury in April and a case in Davidson County. Bond hearings and investigators’ findings At Eatherly’s initial court appearance on May 15 in General Sessions Court, Judge H. Reid Poland III set his bond at $1.25 million and advised him of the potential sentencing ranges, including 15 to 60 years on the attempted murder charge, according to previous reports . Dalton Eatherly, with his left arm wounded, in court on May 21, 2026. (Jazmin Logan) During a May 21 hearing, investigators testified that surveillance cameras captured the confrontation and showed Eatherly attempting to pull a gun from his jacket pocket – not Mace, as he later claimed. They said Fox took Eatherly to the ground during the struggle and that a bullet could be seen ricocheting as the two fell. Seven shell casings were recovered at the scene, all from the same firearm, according to previous reports . | NEWS ALERTS: To get free breaking news alerts on your phone, text the word NEWS to 43414 . Searches of Eatherly’s truck and home revealed a bulletproof vest, a rifle, a shotgun, ammunition, a suspected bag of marijuana and an airline ticket to Istanbul dated May 22. Investigators also recovered his electronic devices, which contained inflammatory racial videos and social media posts referencing lethal force in the weeks leading up to the shooting. No Mace was found at the scene or in his belongings. Poland reset Eatherly’s bond at $1 million , citing state law requiring a higher amount because he was already out on bond in two other cases. Poland also ordered that if released, Eatherly must wear a GPS monitor, relinquish all weapons, abide by a gag order and have any passport application halted or rescinded. He further ruled that no crowdfunding raised after May 13 could be used toward bond, pending a sourcing review in Circuit Court. The case was bound over to the grand jury. Source hearing and most recent bond rulings At a June 3 hearing in Circuit Court , Judge William Goodman III kept Eatherly’s bond at $1 million after hearing conflicting accounts from prosecutors and the defense about what led to the gunfire, according to previous reports . District Attorney General Robert Nash argued that Eatherly provoked the confrontation, saying he had no reason to be at the courthouse that afternoon and had missed a civil hearing earlier that morning. Nash said Eatherly livestreamed the interaction, similar to prior incidents in which he filmed confrontations, and that Fox struck him as the gun came out. Defense attorney Jake Fendley argued that Eatherly acted in self-defense and pointed to his community ties. Fendley also noted that Eatherly failed to appear for a Nashville court hearing earlier that day, resulting in a capias bench warrant, and said he planned to file a motion to dismiss the Davidson County charges. Goodman added a 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. curfew to Eatherly’s release conditions and kept in place earlier orders requiring no weapons, a GPS monitor, a gag order and restrictions on using post–May 13 crowdfunding toward bond. He also denied a motion for LA Bonding to post bail in excess and said Eatherly would need 10 bonding companies to post the full amount – one for every $100,000. According to Davidson County court records, Eatherly also appeared in court on Aug. 6 for charges stemming from a May 9 incident. He was charged there with theft of services $1,000 or less, disorderly conduct and resisting arrest. The court increased his bond to $15,000, noting “the sequence of threatening posts followed by Defendant’s use of a weapon during an altercation, all while on bond in this county, warrant greater oversight,” records said. Eatherly’s bond conditions in Davidson County largely mirror those in the Montgomery County attempted murder case: house arrest, GPS monitor, no weapons or firearms, and a prohibition on entering Davidson County except for scheduled court appearances. The court also ordered that any passport application be stopped or surrendered, and imposed a gag order for case-related information. | GET YOUR LOCAL MORNING NEWS: Sign up for our free daily email newsletter . https://telex.hu/tamogatott-tartalom/202.text: Menü Kereső Több nő kellene a vezetésben: hol akad el Magyarország? Támogatott tartalom Fotó: Tuba Zoltán / Képszerkesztőség Támogatott Tartalom Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Egy férfiak által dominált vállalatnál nem egyszerű nőként érvényesülni a vezetői szinteken. De hogy lehet javítani a nemek arányán? Melyek azok a tulajdonságok, amiket a nők az előnyükre fordíthatnak a szakmai előrejutás során? Segít az esélyegyenlőségen a női kvóták bevezetése? Többek között ezekről a kérdésekről beszélgettünk Csoma Anitával, a Budapesti Corvinus Egyetemen működő executive iskola, a Corvinus SEED oktatójával, az Aspiring Women Leaders program vezetőjével, aki az olajiparban szerzett vezetői tapasztalatával segíti a résztvevőket. Az Aspiring Women Leaders kurzus 2023-ban jött létre, és szeptemberben indul a hatodik osztályunk. Számomra ez egy szívprojekt, hiszen több mint húsz évig dolgoztam az olajiparban, ebből 15 évig mint vezető, és ott elég egyértelműen kijött a nők kisebb aránya a férfiakhoz képest. Nagyon szerettem volna átadni azt a gondolkodásmódot és szükséges tulajdonságokat, amivel Magyarországon és a régióban támogathatjuk a női vezetőket. Ez egy paradox helyzet, ugyanis ahhoz, hogy jó vezetők legyünk, magabiztosnak és erős döntéshozónak kell lennünk, ki kell állnunk a véleményünkért. Mindehhez karakteres jellem szükséges. Ezzel ellentétben a nők legfőbb erőssége – ami nagyban hozzájárul ahhoz, hogy sikeres vezetők legyünk – az empátia és a másokra való odafigyelés. Ez a kettősség különösen nehéz, és ehhez sok nő esetében hozzáadódik a munka és a magánéleti szerepek összehangolásának a kihívása. Egyre kevesebb olyan helyzet adódik, amikor egy nőnek a HR-hez kell fordulnia. Azonban még mindig gyakori a mikroagresszió a vállalatoknál, amikkel együtt élünk. Például amikor egy megbeszélésen nem hagynak minket szóhoz jutni, vagy a szavunkba vágnak, esetleg nem veszik figyelembe a véleményünket. Továbbá rendszeres, hogy nem hallják meg a nők ötletét, csak akkor, ha azt egy férfi kolléga becsomagolja kicsit másképp, és végül az az ő szellemi terméke lesz. Nem látványos dolgokra kell gondolni, amikor a női vezetők kihívásairól beszélünk, hanem apró történetekre, amik egyre sokasodnak, összeadódnak az évek során. Ha a teljesítményt nézzük, nem gondolom, hogy más lenne az elvárás egy női és egy férfi vezetővel szemben. A különbség inkább abban van, hogyan ítéljük meg a vezetői viselkedést. Ahogy azt már említettem, a nőktől gyakran egyszerre várjuk el, hogy empatikusak és odafigyelők, ugyanakkor magabiztosak és erős döntéshozók is legyenek. Csoma Anita – Fotó: Tuba Zoltán / Képszerkesztőség Három nagyon különböző kultúrában dolgoztam mint kutató és vezető. Hollandiában a Shellnél, Houstonban a ConocoPhillipsnél, illetve Magyarországon a MOL-Csoportnál. Az USA-ban például rendkívül teljesítményalapú az egész rendszer, a játékszabályok egyértelműek. Emellett nagyon korán megtanítottak minket arra, hogy nem elég eredményt elérni, azt láthatóvá is kell tenni. Tapasztalatom szerint ez egy olyan készség, amely sok magyar női vezetőnél még fejlesztést igényel: meg kell tanulnunk beszélni az eredményeinkről, és láthatóvá tenni a saját hozzájárulásunkat. Úgy látom, a mi régiónkban a formális játékszabályok és elvárások sokszor kevésbé egyértelműek. A teljesítmény mellett ezért fontos az is, hogy értsük a szervezeten belüli erőviszonyokat, felismerjük, hol és hogyan születnek valójában a döntések. Ez minden vezető számára fontos képesség, de tapasztalatom szerint a női vezetőknek különösen tudatosan kell fejleszteniük. Amikor egy nő vezetői szerepbe kerül, kifejezetten épít a tudásra, és arra, hogy mit tesz le az asztalra. Viszont amikor a következő szintre szeretnénk lépni – például középvezetőből felsővezetői pozícióba –, már nem feltétlenül ugyanaz a szakmai teljesítmény számít, ami addig sikeressé tett minket. Gyakorlatilag át kell kódolnunk a gondolkodásunkat: meg kell értenünk, hogy ezen a szinten mire is van szüksége a vállalatnak vagy annak az intézménynek. Itt már a döntéshozatal és a gazdasági szemlélet jóval nagyobb teret kap. A szocializmus örökségeként régiónkban a nőknek régóta magas a munkaerőpiaci részvétele. Magyarországon a 25–49 éves nők foglalkoztatási rátája ma már közel 85 százalék. A vezetői pozíciók mintegy 41 százalékát nők töltik be. Viszont a legnagyobb probléma az, hogy a legnagyobb tőzsdén jegyzett magyar vállalatok igazgatóságaiban már csak körülbelül 13 százalék a nők aránya. Mindez azt jelenti, hogy míg a nők nagy számban vannak jelen a munkaerőpiacon és a vezetésben is, a legfelső vállalati döntéshozói szinten az arányuk drasztikusan lecsökken. Egy igazgatóságban tíz emberből alig több mint egy nő, miközben az európai átlagban nagyjából minden harmadik igazgatósági tag nő. Ez óriási különbség. Viccesen tyúkanyó-szindrómának szoktam nevezni ezt a jelenséget. Mi, nők, nagyon jók vagyunk abban, hogy odafigyeljünk az embereinkre, támogassuk őket, és húzzuk előre a szervezetet. Azonban akadnak olyan női vezetők – és ezt a program résztvevőinek tapasztalatai is alátámasztják –, akik érzelmileg szinte egyesülnek a csapatukkal, és így nehezebben hozzák meg az embereket érintő, kevésbé pozitív döntéseket. Az empátia a varázspálcánk, de a felsővezetői szintre lépésnél a határhúzás borzasztóan fontos. Több szerepjátékot is használunk a képzésen. Például az empátiával kapcsolatban azt a példát vesszük, hogy egy beosztottunk bejön hozzánk, elmeséli, milyen problémája van otthon, és erre hogyan tudunk reagálni. Lehet úgy is, hogy elmondjuk, mennyire sajnáljuk, és szinte átvesszük az érzéseit – ilyenkor elmosódhat a határ köztem és a kollégám közt. Vagy lehet úgy is, hogy „hallom, amit mondasz, nagyon köszönöm, hogy megosztottad velem. Hogyan tudok segíteni?” Van különbség. Egy kétszer kétnapos programról van szó, ahol az időpontok között mentorálás zajlik, majd egy közös eseménnyel zárjuk a négy hónapos képzést. Az első nap az önismeretről szól, arról, hogy mik az erősségeink, mi az, amivel motiváljuk a csapatunkat. A második napon ráfordulunk arra, hogy hová is szeretnénk eljutni, mi az aspirációnk, és megfogalmazzuk a programhoz kapcsolódó céljainkat. A harmadik-negyedik napon pedig erősen a vezetői jelenlétre koncentrálunk, hogyan jelenünk meg az igazgatósági üléseken, és hogy mit is jelent a bizalom. Ezen túl átvesszük, hogyan építhetünk kapcsolati hálót, kik azok az emberek, akik megtartanak és támogatnak minket, legyen szó mentorokról, szponzorokról vagy más fontos kapcsolatokról. A program egyik különleges értéke, hogy a résztvevők egymást is támogatják, és valódi közösség alakul ki közöttük. A mostani őszi kurzussal együtt már több mint ötven nő vett részt a programban. Rendszerint férfidominált területekről – például az energiaiparból, az IT-szektorból és ügyvédi irodákból – érkeznek hozzánk, és azt látjuk, hogy a négy hónap alatt sokkal tudatosabbá válnak abban, hogyan szeretnének vezetőként továbblépni. Fotó: Tuba Zoltán / Képszerkesztőség Van, hogy valaki a kurzus során érzi elérkezettnek az időt arra, hogy megpályázza a következő vezetői szintet. Más éppen nálunk ismeri fel, hogy bár a vállalata felfelé terelné, ő tudatosan a jelenlegi szinten szeretne maradni. Számomra mindkettő siker. A lényeg, hogy legyen bátorságuk felismerni és kimondani, hogy mit akarnak, és meghúzni a határaikat. A Corvinus-SEED-ben azt tanítjuk, hogy a vezetés tanulható, és a programjaink tapasztalatai is ezt támasztják alá. Engem inkább az a kérdés foglalkoztat, hogy milyen szakmai háttérből vezet az út a legfelső vezetői szintekre. Geológusként a STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics, azaz tudomány, technológia, mérnöki tudomány és matematika) területéről érkezem, és azt látom, hogy a hasonló szakmai háttérrel rendelkező nők ritkábban jelennek meg a legfelső vezetői szinteken. Az igazgatóságokban gyakrabban találkozunk például pénzügyi vagy HR-háttérrel rendelkező nőkkel. Ez felvet egy számomra izgalmas kérdést: vajon valóban a vezetői készségek hiányoznak, vagy bizonyos szakmai pályákról egyszerűen nehezebb eljutni oda, ahol már az egész vállalatról kell gondolkodni? Van, hogy egy boardban szeretnék a diverzitást javítani, vagy meg akarnak felelni a kvótáknak. Azt szoktam mondani, hogy a hangsúly nem azon van, hogy egy kolléga nő, hanem azon, hogy olyan embereket keressünk, akik másképpen gondolkodnak, mint az igazgatóság többi tagja. Kvótahívő vagyok, de erről rengeteg vita zajlik. Azt látom, hogy a kvóta arra jó, hogy felhívja a figyelmet egy helyzetre. Az olaszok, a franciák és a skandináv országok már korábban bevezették a kvótákat, és ott az igazgatótanácsokban lévő női vezetők aránya az európai átlag felett van. Ahol azonban később jelent meg a kvóta, ott egyértelműen érzékelhető a lemaradás a nemek arányát illetően. Véleményem szerint az egyes szervezetek felelőssége, hogy a kvóták mentén hozott döntéseket transzparensen és következetesen kommunikálják. Ha világos, hogy miért van szükség a kvótára, és milyen szempontok alapján születnek a döntések, jóval kevesebb vita és ellenállás övezi ezt a kérdést. Természetesen hosszú távon nem kvótákban szeretnék gondolkodni, hanem egyénekre fókuszálni. A cél nem az, hogy minden üggyel a HR-hez menjünk. Ha például egy férfi kolléga megkérdezi tőlünk, hogy nőként csak dekorációnak hívtak-e meg minket egy megbeszélésre – ahogy ez egy IT-szektorban dolgozó részvevőnkkel megtörtént –, akkor többféleképpen is reagálhatunk. Bepanaszolhatjuk az illetőt, de csendben is maradhatunk, vagy – ahogy azt a programban tanítom – reagálhatunk egy kérdéssel is: „Miért gondolja és miért mondja ezt? Fejtse ki”. Ezzel lehetőséget teremtünk arra, hogy a másik fél elgondolkodjon a saját sémáin és azon, ami történt. Magunk mellé állíthatjuk a férfi munkatársainkat: a változáshoz nem a két nem szembeállítására, hanem együttműködésre, harmóniára van szükség. https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026.text: Chantemekki Fortson, mother of Roger Fortson, holds a photo of her son during a news conference on 9 May 2024 in Fort Walton Beach, Florida. Photograph: Gerald Herbert/AP View image in fullscreen Chantemekki Fortson, mother of Roger Fortson, holds a photo of her son during a news conference on 9 May 2024 in Fort Walton Beach, Florida. Photograph: Gerald Herbert/AP Florida Florida jury finds ex-sheriff’s deputy not guilty in shooting death of Black air force airman Roger Fortson was shot by deputy when he opened door with gun in hand after a false domestic disturbance call Marina Dunbar Sat 3 Oct 2026 12.44 EDT Last modified on Sat 3 Oct 2026 12.45 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A Florida jury recently found former sheriff’s deputy Eddie Duran not guilty of manslaughter with a firearm in the fatal shooting of Roger Fortson, a Black US air force airman who was killed inside his apartment after authorities responded to an unfounded report of a domestic disturbance. An Okaloosa county jury acquitted Duran, 38, on Thursday after about two hours of deliberations. He had faced up to 30 years in prison if convicted. Duran, who is Hispanic, was an Okaloosa county sheriff’s deputy in May 2024 when he was sent to Fortson’s apartment in Fort Walton Beach where Fortson – originally from Atlanta – was stationed. Former Dallas police officer convicted of murdering Black neighbor given early parole Read more Authorities have said Duran was directed to the apartment after a report of a domestic disturbance that turned out to be false. After Duran repeatedly knocked on the door, Fortson answered while holding a handgun at his side with the weapon pointed toward the ground. Authorities say Duran fired multiple times before telling Fortson to drop the gun. The encounter was captured on the deputy’s body camera. Thursday’s verdict came after a four-day trial. One day after Duran was acquitted, civil rights attorney Ben Crump said that Fortson’s family would continue its legal fight and vowed to “seek accountability” through the civil court system for the 2024 shooting. While the criminal prosecution has ended with Duran’s acquittal, a federal civil rights lawsuit filed by Fortson’s family remains pending. “Roger’s life and his service will always matter,” Crump said in a statement on Friday. “His family will keep fighting for him, and we will stand with them as they pursue their civil rights case in federal court and seek accountability for the tragic loss of his life.” Duran was fired from the Okaloosa sheriff’s office after killing Fortson. His defense attorney argued that the former deputy was “doing his job” and said Fortson would still be alive if he had not armed himself before answering the door. Fortson’s mother, Chantemekki Fortson, told the Atlanta news outlet WXIA she was unsurprised by the verdict, citing the speed of the jury’s deliberations. “They went to deliberate for just two hours,” she said. “So, again, I wasn’t surprised.” She also said the trial forced her to face details surrounding her son’s death that she had spent the previous two years trying to avoid. “Now I can’t do that,” she told WXIA. “Like he’s really gone. “He’s never coming back. He’s never gonna say, ‘Mom, what you doing? Mom, you wanna go get something to eat? Mom, you need do your hair.’ Like I’m never going to hear my baby’s voice no more.” Explore more on these topics Florida US crime US justice system Atlanta US policing news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness

https://www.dw.com/en/nord-stream-trial-.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OFyA Serhii Kuznietsov's defense team argued that the alleged actions should not be deemed a criminal act Image: Markus Scholz/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement The trial of a former Ukrainian special forces officer, Serhii Kuznietsov, opened in the northern German city of Hamburg on Wednesday amid considerable public and press interest. Kuznietsov is accused of leading the September 2022 sabotage operation that put the undersea Nord Stream 1 and 2 gas pipelines linking Russian to Germany out of action . The pipelines remain inactive four years later, with no sign of plans to ever reactivate them as Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine heads into its fifth winter. Prosecutors accuse the Ukrainian of participation in a war crime by targeting civilian infrastructure, but his defense lawyers on Wednesday argued that the case should be dismissed entirely on multiple grounds. The defense lawyers argue that the case should be thrown out entirely, saying their client is forbidden from speaking with them or anybody else about the case Image: Markus Scholz/dpa/picture alliance What did Kuznietsov's lawyers say on opening day? A team of three lawyers representing Kuznietsov questioned the premise of the trial in court. One of Kuznietsov's lawyers, Nicola Canestrini, argued that it was not valid to try the officer on war crimes charges for an attack on civilian infrastructure. He argued that the pipeline, which provided half of Germany's natural gas imports prior to Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, was ultimately a " Russian weapon," given the importance of energy revenues for funding Moscow's military. "Is it unlawful to destroy an aggressor's infrastructure without harming any human beings?" Canestrini asked the court. After the charges were read out, the judge asked Kuznietsov if he wanted to comment, and he said that he did not. His lawyers argue that this silence extends beyond not speaking in court and say this should be the main grounds for dismissal. They say Kuznietsov is sworn to secrecy by his home government in Ukraine and so is unable to discuss his case or potential exonerating evidence with anyone, including his legal representatives. "He is not permitted to speak. His two immediate superiors told him that he does not have authorization to make any statements — not even to his lawyers," defense attorney Jes Meyer-Lohkamp told the court. In German law, Meyer-Lohkamp argued: "Anyone who cannot speak out cannot be convicted." A small group of demonstrators stood outside the court on Wednesday arguing that the wrong party to the war in Ukraine was on trial Image: Markus Scholz/dpa/picture alliance What was the mood in court in Hamburg? DW's Matthew Moore was on hand in the court in northern Germany on Wednesday. There is huge interest in this court case, Moore reported. No sooner had the court doors opened at 07:30 local time in Hamburg than the first journalists, observers and protesters began arriving. A small pro-Ukraine protest held up a banner saying, "Russia is a terrorist." One participant from Germany told Moore they wanted to remind the world of "the war crimes taking place against the Ukrainian people." Inside, a Ukrainian student told DW that he and others had made the journey from Kyiv to show support for the defendant, Serhii Kuznietsov. "Serhii Kuznietsov is a hero," the student said. In the eyes of the German prosecutors, it is another matter. They accuse him of carrying out a war crime. If found guilty of his part in the gas pipeline bombing, Kuznietsov faces a lengthy prison sentence. Based on investigative reporting and a Bojan Pancevski book on the sabotage published this year, Kuznietsov coordinated a small and unlikely team made up not of professional spies or soldiers, but rather people with relevant specialist skills like deep-sea divers and explosives experts Image: Markus Scholz/dpa/picture alliance Geramny's Wadephul: 'We will deal with any outcome' The case has been highly politically awkward for Germany — a staunch supporter of Ukraine despite investigators pursuing a trail that led to Kuznietsov and other suspects. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has repeatedly denied any Ukrainian involvement in the operation , and had also resisted Kuznietsov's extradition to Germany after his arrest in Italy last year , arguing that there was no case to answer. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul declined to comment on the trial on Wednesday, saying that the most important thing for now was for the case to proceed with no political interference or restrictions. "We will deal with any outcome, and we will, of course, take it into account in our political calculations," he told a press conference in Berlin. https://www.jns.org/feature/israels-poli.text: Passing a comprehensive draft law to shield yeshivah students from compulsory military service is the central demand of both lists. Shas and United Torah Judaism (UTJ) enter the Oct. 27 Knesset election seeking lasting protection for their religious institutions and communities. The two parties won 18 seats in 2022, supplying more than a quarter of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s original 64-seat coalition. That partnership is now tested by the unresolved dispute over Haredi military service. The parties Although commonly grouped together as the Haredi, or ultra-Orthodox, parties, Shas and UTJ emerged from different communities and represent distinct political traditions. Shas entered national politics in 1984 under the spiritual leadership of Rabbi Ovadia Yosef, a former Sephardi chief rabbi. Its founders sought independent representation for Sephardi Haredim who felt marginalized within the predominantly Ashkenazi religious establishment. The party joined the defense of religious observance and education to a broader mission of restoring Sephardi religious prestige and representing disadvantaged families. That combination gave Shas an electorate extending beyond the yeshivah community. Its appeal reached traditional Sephardi and Mizrachi Israelis who identified with Yosef’s religious authority and the party’s social agenda without adopting a strictly Haredi lifestyle. Israel Democracy Institute (IDI) researcher Gilad Malach wrote that Shas is “a party open to a broad group of traditional voters rather than just the ultra-Orthodox community.” Aryeh Deri leads Shas politically, with Yinon Azoulay second on its submitted electoral list. Political leadership operates under the authority of the Council of Torah Sages, which provides the party’s religious direction. Rabbi Yitzhak Yosef, Ovadia Yosef’s son and himself a former Sephardi chief rabbi, is a prominent spiritual figure in the current leadership. UTJ, meanwhile, brings together two branches of Ashkenazi Haredi society. Agudat Yisrael principally represents Chassidic communities, while Degel HaTorah represents the Lithuanian, non-Chassidic tradition. Rabbi Elazar Menachem Man Shach established Degel HaTorah in 1988 after disputes over representation within the Chassidic-dominated Agudat Yisrael. The two began contesting national elections jointly in 1992, pooling their electoral strength while retaining separate organizations and rabbinical authorities. That structure continues to shape UTJ’s leadership. Yaakov Asher heads its electoral list, followed by Agudat Yisrael leader Yitzhak Goldknopf. Asher’s rise follows Rabbi Dov Lando’s decision that veteran Degel HaTorah lawmakers Moshe Gafni and Uri Maklev would not seek reelection. Lando is Degel HaTorah’s senior spiritual leader. The change shows that politicians remain accountable to religious authorities who determine their representation and political boundaries. The platform Passing a comprehensive draft law to shield yeshivah students from compulsory military service is the central demand of both parties. Their leaders regard sustained religious study as a contribution to Jewish continuity that the state should support. Shas and Degel HaTorah have shown greater willingness than Agudat Yisrael to negotiate recruitment targets and limited financial sanctions for a potential bill. In late 2025, Degel HaTorah backed a bill that would let eligible yeshivah students defer service while studying until receiving an exemption at age 26, alongside recruitment targets for the wider Haredi population. It would not require every student to serve before receiving that exemption. Agudat Yisrael has taken a harder line against targets and sanctions. All three oppose compulsory service for full-time yeshivah students. Rabbi Yitzhak Yosef has also opposed drafting students experiencing a “crisis” in their studies, while clarifying that he was not referring to all Haredim outside full-time study. On education, both parties seek public funding for yeshivahs and Haredi schools while defending their educational autonomy, including funding for institutions that do not teach the full core curriculum of subjects such as mathematics and English. Their economic priorities extend to childcare subsidies, family assistance and housing. Shas places particular emphasis on low-income households and food assistance; Deri made resolving a food-voucher funding dispute a condition for supporting the budget in late 2025. UTJ emphasizes expanding housing suited to Haredi communities. On religion and state, both parties seek to preserve Orthodox authority over marriage, conversion and religious services, oppose civil marriage and resist expanded public transportation on Shabbat. These policies shape religious arrangements for the wider population as well as their own constituents. Their support for restricting judicial intervention is closely connected to these priorities: court rulings have affected conscription arrangements, institutional funding and religious policy. Both have backed limits on the High Court’s power to overturn legislation and government decisions. Security positions are less central to their programs but remain consequential. Shas opposes Palestinian statehood and has backed settlement expansion in Judea and Samaria. On Gaza, Deri has supported dismantling Hamas while also backing negotiated ceasefires and hostage releases. UTJ has no unified territorial platform, and its factions differ: Agudat Yisrael’s Goldknopf has advocated extending Israeli sovereignty and reestablishing Jewish settlements in Gaza, while Degel HaTorah’s Gafni has opposed resettling Gaza. These differences make it difficult to assign UTJ a single position on territorial policy, even as both factions cooperate with parties advocating settlement expansion. The partners Shas and UTJ have long helped anchor Netanyahu’s governing bloc, but the conscription dispute has strained that partnership. In July 2025, UTJ left the government and coalition after negotiations failed to secure exemptions for yeshivah students. Shas withdrew its ministers two days later but remained in the coalition, subsequently resigning from its parliamentary coalition posts in October that year. Both sought to pressure Netanyahu, though they differed over how far to distance themselves from his government. They enter this election maintaining their own alliance. On Oct. 11, the parties signed a surplus-vote agreement, which can help one of them secure an additional seat. They also pledged continued cooperation over educational funding, conscription legislation and state religious institutions. That coordination does not settle whom they will support for prime minister. On Oct. 13, Deri told Kan Moreshet he favored a broad government including Yashar Party leader Gadi Eisenkot, led by Netanyahu. Asher has publicly expressed willingness to serve in a government led by Eisenkot. However, Meir Porush, number four on the UTJ list, rejected such a possibility, arguing in an Oct. 5 radio interview that Netanyahu-aligned parties are more sympathetic to Haredi religious and communal interests. Their statements reflect UTJ’s competing impulses to preserve its established partnership and consider alternatives. Those alternatives carry significant obstacles. Eisenkot advocates broad Haredi conscription. His bloc supports conditioning school funding on a full core curriculum. Most parties in it also favor prioritizing those who serve and work for government benefits. An agreement would require compromises on educational autonomy and public assistance. UTJ’s stated conditions also limit postponing the draft question until after a government takes office. Porush said its two factions had agreed not to accept ministerial or committee leadership positions, or support coalition legislation, until the status of yeshivah students was resolved in law. Coalition promises alone would not secure the party’s full participation. Shas and UTJ face competition from both their right-wing allies and smaller Haredi lists. Challengers, such as the Haredi Public Party, are competing for dissatisfied Haredi voters. IDI analysis found that 11% of self-identified Haredi voters backed Likud or Religious Zionism-Otzma Yehudit in 2022. An Oct. 11 Kan News poll projected seven seats for Shas and eight for UTJ, three fewer than in 2022. Retaining their electorate is essential to preserving their bargaining power in the next Knesset.
